links.comparator_used: Expert clinician evaluation of the same summaries using the same criteria (relevance, completeness, redundancy, coherence and structure, grammar and terminology, hallucinations)
links.outcome: Agreement between LLM-judge/automatic metric scores and expert ratings of medical summary quality
links.effect: Pearson correlation between summary quality score and expert opinions was 0.688 for relevance; neither metrics nor LLM judges were reliable for hallucinations (no other numbers in the abstract)
links.tradeoff: New failure mode: LLM judges and automatic metrics missed factual errors and semantic distortions (hallucinations), so full automation of evaluation remains challenging and expert review is still needed for flagged cases.
links.quote: In terms of relevance, the Pearson correlation between the summary quality score and the expert opinions was 0.688.

design_hint: automated quality control of LLM summaries (LLM-as-a-judge and automatic metrics) versus expert review
